matcher: vedagraph.domain.mentions -- whole folded token, not a prefix
why_word_forms_and_not_a_prefix: The Wave 2 ritual registry fixed this by admitting `yupa` as a four-letter word-initial PREFIX. The mention layer that actually writes MENTIONS_ENTITY matches whole folded tokens, so a prefix never fires there -- and `yupa` with a short a would in any case miss `yupan` and `yupe`, whose stem vowel is long. The attested word forms are registered instead.

deliberately_not_registered.dhariyūpīyāyāṁ: RV 6.27.5. The place-name Hariyupiya. GAP-RITUAL-003's own evidence names it: 'Eleven mantras carry a yupa-word (one of them the place-name Hariyupiya)'.
deliberately_not_registered.sthūrayūpavat: RV 8.23.24. A medial compound, 'having a stout post', used as an epithet. Left out because the mention layer matches whole tokens and registering a compound whose head is the post is a separate decision from registering its inflections.
deliberately_not_registered.aśvayūpāya: RV 1.162.6 and VSM 25.29. A medial compound. Both mantras are already reached by yupavraska and yupavahas in the same verse, so registering it would add no passage and would take a decision this artifact does not need to take.
deliberately_not_registered.yūpavāhāścaṣālaṃ: A sandhi-glued token produced by transliterating the VSM container text. Its content is already reached by yupavahas in the parallel text of the same verse.

host_form_audit: Printed per alias, not per row. Every host form of every proposed alias is a yupa form; no alias reaches a different word.
